narration: Welcome to the Central Asian Antiquities gallery. This is the Tibetan Prayer Wheel, accession number NM 85.4/7, a hand‑held object from the 19th‑20th century, crafted of metal, shell and wood. It stands about 22 centimetres tall and is adorned with auspicious Buddhist symbols. Inside, a tightly wound paper scroll repeats the mantra “Om mani padme hum” many times; spinning the wheel is believed to release the mantra’s merit into the world, just as if it were spoken aloud. The wheel’s delicate construction and spiritual purpose offer a glimpse into Himalayan devotional practices that continue to inspire visitors today.
